title: YNAB Alternatives 2026: Prices and Plans Compared
h1: YNAB Alternatives 2026: Prices and Plans Compared
metaDescription: Compare YNAB alternatives including Monarch Money, Quicken Simplifi, Goodbudget, Tiller, PocketGuard, and Copilot Money with published prices and plans.
intro:
Goodbudget, Quicken Simplifi, PocketGuard, Tiller, Monarch Money, and Copilot Money are six YNAB alternatives, with published prices ranging from a $0 free tier on Goodbudget to $199.99 per year on Monarch Money Plus. At The Modern Wallet, we lay out the arithmetic behind subscription costs and feature tiers so people can compare yearly software expenses accurately.

[YNAB](https://www.ynab.com/pricing) charges $109 United States Dollars (USD) per year when paid annually, which equals $9.08 per month, or $14.99 per month on its monthly plan, plus sales tax where applicable. YNAB pairs account connections with a budgeting method where users assign every dollar a job. A single YNAB subscription can be shared with up to six people across partners, families, and close-knit groups, and new signups start with a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card.

For readers exploring broader tools, our [best budgeting apps roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps/) covers general category options, and our [best budgeting apps for couples roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps-for-couples/) compares account-sharing setups. If you want to calculate categories before selecting software, see our [zero-based budget calculator](/budget/zero-based-budget-calculator/) and our guide on [how to make a budget](/guides/how-to-make-a-budget/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a YNAB Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting an alternative to YNAB depends on five clear criteria: the underlying budgeting method, bank connectivity, the billing structure, trial terms, and the user interface. YNAB relies on a budgeting method where users assign every dollar a job and connect accounts. Goodbudget uses envelope budgeting, while Quicken Simplifi uses Spending Plan budgeting.

Tiller puts account data into a spreadsheet automatically using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel. 

Subscription costs and commitments vary across providers. PocketGuard sells a Lifetime access option for a single payment of $149.99 alongside its $74.99 annual subscription. Quicken Simplifi lists an annual rate of $3.99 per month ($47.88 per year) against a regular rate of $6.99 per month ($83.88 per year). Goodbudget maintains a $0 free plan with limited envelopes, whereas Monarch Money sells Core at $99.99 per year and Plus at $199.99 per year.

Trial periods also differ before billing begins. YNAB offers a 34-day free trial without collecting payment card details. Tiller provides a 30-day trial followed by an additional 30-day money-back window. PocketGuard and Monarch Money provide 7-day trials, while Copilot Money does not display a monthly billing price on its main pricing page.

Check these factors when evaluating options:

- Does the software support automatic bank synchronization or manual entry?
- Does the subscription cover multiple people, or must each person pay separately?
- Is the budgeting system based on envelope assignments, flexible spending plans, or spreadsheets?
- Does the platform offer a one-time purchase option, an ongoing monthly fee, or an annual renewal?

alternatives.heading: Monarch Money Core and Plus Plans Versus YNAB
alternatives.body:
Monarch Money offers two annual subscriptions: Core at $99.99 per year (or $14.99 per month) and Plus at $199.99 per year. Monarch Money advertises an ad-free service, states that it never sells customer financial data, and offers a money-back guarantee. The Plus tier adds cash flow forecasting, multi-source income tracking, and deeper investment analysis. The service recommends signing up on the web and provides a 7-day trial.

Monarch Money fits individuals looking for multiple income tracking, investment tracking, and forecasting without commercial advertisements.

Monarch Money falls short of YNAB on trial duration, and does not list group sharing on its pricing page. YNAB includes sharing for up to six people on a standard $109 annual subscription and provides a 34-day trial without asking for a credit card, while Monarch Money offers a 7-day trial.

A full year of Monarch Money Core paid monthly costs $179.88 (12 months at $14.99), matching the $179.88 annual cost of YNAB monthly. Billed annually, Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year, which is $9.01 lower than YNAB's $109 annual fee. Upgrading to Monarch Money Plus raises the annual bill to $199.99, which is $90.99 higher than YNAB's annual plan.

alternatives.heading: Copilot Money Annual Subscription and Apple Integrations
alternatives.body:
Copilot Money charges $9 per month billed annually at $109 under a limited-time promotional rate, compared to a regular annual price of $119. Copilot Money runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and web platforms, connects with more than 16,000 banks, and includes human customer support alongside a money assistant. Copilot Money emphasizes that its plan has no tiers, no add-ons, and no AI credits, while noting that its Households sharing feature is coming soon.



Copilot Money falls short of YNAB on platform availability and household collaboration. Copilot Money lists only iPhone, iPad, Mac, and web platforms, does not list a monthly billing price on its page, and notes Households is coming soon. YNAB supports sharing for up to six people today.

On annual billing, Copilot Money's current $109 price matches YNAB's $109 yearly rate dollar for dollar. If Copilot Money returns to its regular $119 annual price, it costs $10 more per year than YNAB.

alternatives.heading: Quicken Simplifi Annual Pricing and Cash Flow Projections
alternatives.body:
Quicken Simplifi provides spending plan budgeting, net worth tracking, and cash flow projections looking up to 12 months into the future. The software connects to over 14,000 financial institutions across web and mobile platforms and includes free one-on-one setup help from Quicken specialists. The published rate is $3.99 per month billed annually, against a regular list price of $6.99 per month.

Quicken Simplifi fits budgeters who want cash flow forecasting, net worth tracking, and setup help from Quicken experts.

Quicken Simplifi falls short of YNAB on budgeting philosophy and trial flexibility. Simplifi uses Spending Plan budgeting rather than assigning every dollar a job, does not list a monthly billing plan on its page, and does not list a free trial.

At the promotional $3.99 monthly rate billed annually, Quicken Simplifi costs $47.88 for the first year. That is $61.12 lower than YNAB's $109 annual subscription. At Simplifi's regular $6.99 monthly rate billed annually, the total comes to $83.88 per year, which remains $25.12 lower than YNAB.

alternatives.heading: PocketGuard Lifetime, Annual, and Monthly Options
alternatives.body:
PocketGuard provides subscription plans with priority human support and AI chat included. The pricing page offers three payment options: Monthly at $12.99 per month, Premium Yearly at $74.99 per year ($6.25 per month, which PocketGuard notes saves $81 per year compared to monthly billing), and a Lifetime plan for a single payment of $149.99. All three payment options include a 7-day free trial.



PocketGuard falls short of YNAB on subscription sharing and trial length. PocketGuard does not advertise multi-user family sharing for up to six accounts under a single fee, and its trial lasts 7 days compared to YNAB's 34 days.

Over one year, PocketGuard Premium Yearly costs $74.99, saving $34.01 compared to YNAB's $109 annual fee. Paying PocketGuard monthly costs $155.88 per year (12 times $12.99), which is $24.00 less than YNAB's $179.88 monthly total. Over two years, PocketGuard Lifetime at $149.99 costs $68.01 less than paying $218.00 for two years of YNAB.

alternatives.heading: Tiller Automated Spreadsheets for Google Sheets and Excel
alternatives.body:
Tiller puts account data into a spreadsheet automatically using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel. Tiller costs $99 per year, with no advertisements or hidden fees, plus sales tax where applicable. New users receive a 30-day free trial where payment cards are not charged until the trial ends, followed by a 30-day money-back guarantee that provides up to 60 days of risk-free evaluation.

Tiller fits budgeters who prefer managing budgets inside Google Sheets or Excel spreadsheets.

Tiller falls short of YNAB on standalone app budgeting workflows. Tiller puts account data into a spreadsheet automatically, whereas YNAB provides an app where users assign every dollar a job.

Billed annually, Tiller costs $99 per year, which is $10.00 less than YNAB's $109 annual fee. Tiller offers no monthly subscription plan, whereas YNAB allows customers to pay month to month at $14.99.

alternatives.heading: Goodbudget Envelope Budgeting and Free Tier
alternatives.body:
Goodbudget brings envelope budgeting to web, Android, and iPhone devices. Goodbudget offers a Free plan costing $0 that includes 10 regular envelopes, 10 more envelopes, 1 account, 2 devices, 1 year of transaction history, debt tracking, and community support. Goodbudget Premium costs $10 per month or $80 per year, adding automatic bank synchronization for US institutions, unlimited envelopes, unlimited accounts, 5 devices, 7 years of history, and email support.

Goodbudget fits budgeters who want envelope budgeting without paying a subscription fee, as well as those seeking an $80 annual plan.

Goodbudget falls short of YNAB on bank synchronization scope and sharing limits. The Free plan lacks automatic bank sync entirely, and Goodbudget Premium limits bank synchronization to US banks across a maximum of 5 devices, whereas YNAB supports up to 6 users with shared plans.

A user on Goodbudget Free pays $0 per year. Upgrading to Goodbudget Premium billed annually costs $80 per year, which is $29.00 lower than YNAB's $109 fee. Paying Goodbudget Premium monthly costs $120.00 over 12 months, saving $59.88 compared to YNAB's $179.88 monthly rate.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
This comparison focuses strictly on consumer personal budgeting and cash flow software. Those looking for small business accounting tools can review dedicated alternatives platforms in our [financial comparisons hub](/compare/).

Additionally, budgeters who prefer physical cash systems without any digital tools do not need paid budgeting applications.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on YNAB Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Several pricing moves or feature updates would alter the cost-benefit balance between YNAB and these alternatives:

- YNAB adjusting its $109 annual or $14.99 monthly subscription fees, or modifying its six-person sharing feature.
- Copilot Money publishing a standard monthly billing option or launching its shared Households feature.
- Quicken Simplifi removing its $3.99 promotional discount and shifting all new customers to the $6.99 monthly rate ($83.88 per year).
- PocketGuard changing its $149.99 Lifetime access price or modifying its $74.99 yearly subscription.
- Goodbudget altering the envelope or account restrictions on its $0 Free tier, or expanding automatic bank sync beyond US banks.
- Monarch Money modifying the $99.99 Core or $199.99 Plus annual price points.

stillBetterFit.heading: When YNAB Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
YNAB remains the better option for households committed to assigning every dollar a job who want to share a single subscription. The application requires users to assign every dollar a job and connect accounts. Because one YNAB subscription supports up to six people for $109 per year, a group sharing the plan divides that single annual cost.

YNAB also provides a 34-day free trial that does not require entering a credit card upfront.

verdict:
Goodbudget provides a $0 free tier among these options, while Quicken Simplifi lists a promotional annual cost of $47.88 per year. PocketGuard offers a $149.99 Lifetime plan, Tiller provides automatic imports directly into spreadsheets for $99 per year, and Monarch Money Core matches YNAB's monthly rate while charging $99.99 annually. YNAB provides a budgeting method where users assign every dollar a job with sharing for up to six people at $109 per year.

To pick the best option for your household, identify whether you prefer envelope allocation or automated spending summaries, verify your device platform requirements, and compare total annual subscription costs in our table.

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to YNAB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Goodbudget provides a $0 Free plan that includes 10 regular envelopes, 10 additional envelopes, 1 financial account, 2 devices, debt tracking, and 1 year of transaction history.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest YNAB alternative?
faqs.answer: Goodbudget Free costs $0. Among paid annual subscriptions, Quicken Simplifi lists a promotional price of $3.99 per month billed annually ($47.88 per year), while its regular list price is $6.99 per month ($83.88 per year). PocketGuard also offers an annual plan at $74.99 per year.

faqs.question: Does YNAB have a free trial?
faqs.answer: Yes. YNAB offers a 34-day free trial that does not require entering a credit card at signup.

faqs.question: How does YNAB pricing compare to Monarch Money?
faqs.answer: On monthly billing, both YNAB and Monarch Money Core cost $14.99 per month ($179.88 per year). On annual billing, Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year, while YNAB costs $109 per year. Monarch Money also offers a Plus tier at $199.99 per year.

faqs.question: Which alternative uses envelope budgeting?
faqs.answer: Goodbudget uses envelope budgeting. It provides envelope budgeting on its $0 Free plan and its $80 annual Premium plan.
